extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, agents/brokers/web-brokers, QHP issuers, and State health officials
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and proposed standards for State-based Exchange Enhanced Direct Enrollment (SBE-EDE) implementation, treatment of State-required benefits relative to Essential Health Benefits (EHB), and standards of conduct and documentation requirements for agents, brokers, and web-brokers assisting with Exchange enrollments.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBE-EDE web-broker consumer data protections
rubrics_metrics.description: All consumer data collected, stored, or transmitted through web-broker platforms operating under the SBE-EDE option would remain subject to the privacy and security standards established at §155.260, and web-brokers participating in the SBE-EDE option would be subject to HHS oversight and monitoring pursuant to §155.280 as a non-Exchange entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Exchanges implementing SBE-EDE would be required to ensure web-brokers comply with these protections, including, but not limited to, encryption, access controls, and audit logging requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS oversight via §155.1200 (SMART reporting and audits)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would maintain oversight authority over State Exchanges under §155.1200, relying on the State-based Marketplace Annual Reporting Tool (SMART) as a key oversight mechanism; State Exchanges are required to complete SMART submissions annually and engage independent qualified auditing entities to perform annual external financial and programmatic audits included with SMART submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS would review SMART submissions, issue formal letters summarizing observations and required corrective actions, and use this SMART-based compliance monitoring (plus additional TA and communications) as safeguards to mitigate program integrity risks under SBE-EDE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange Blueprint submission timeline and review
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly-transitioning or approved State Exchange must submit an Exchange Blueprint application, or Blueprint revision, to HHS for review at least 15 months prior to the targeted open enrollment launch date as an SBE-EDE; for approved State Exchanges, this is considered a significant change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following submission of a revised Exchange Blueprint application in accordance with §155.105(e), HHS would have up to 90 days to review the revision and approve or deny the change; approved State Exchanges must also request HHS approval for significant changes to their single, streamlined eligibility application under §155.405.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational readiness demonstration for SBE-EDE (§155.221(k)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Exchange that wants to implement the SBE-EDE option would be required to demonstrate to HHS operational readiness for the State Exchange to enroll qualified individuals in a QHP in a manner that constitutes enrollment through the Exchange and to enable individuals to apply for APTC and cost sharing and receive Medicaid and CHIP assessments/determinations using the eligibility application described in §155.405.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This demonstration is a condition of HHS approval to be considered an SBE-EDE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation plan and timeline requirement (§155.221(k)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must provide HHS with an implementation plan and timeline that details key activities, milestones, and its communications and outreach strategy to support the transition of enrollment operations to EDE entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is to ensure HHS and the State can coordinate details to maximize the chances of a successful transition to SBE-EDE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum EDE partner capability (§155.221(k)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would not approve a State Exchange to implement SBE-EDE unless the State Exchange demonstrates that at least one EDE entity selected by the State is capable of enrolling all consumers in the State and meets minimum Federal requirements to participate in the FFE's EDE program, including requirements at §§155.220 and 155.221 and accessibility requirements under §155.205(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no EDE partner meets these requirements, the State Exchange would be required to continue operation of its own consumer-facing State Exchange website for eligibility and enrollment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange business controls and partnering flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges electing to implement SBE-EDE would retain flexibility to determine their own business controls while complying with §155.220(n) and §155.221(j), which outline applicability of Federal web-broker and EDE requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes compliance with standardized website disclaimers, web-broker operational readiness, business audit and security and privacy documentation, and display of website changes; State Exchanges could partner with existing HHS-approved web-broker EDE partners as a starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of State-required benefits 'in addition to EHB' (proposed §155.170(a) revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State-required benefits would be considered 'in addition to EHB' (and thus not an EHB) if they are: required by a State action taking place after December 31, 2011; applicable to the small group and/or individual markets; specific to required care, treatment, or services; and not required by State action for purposes of compliance with Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal would add these four conjunctive elements explicitly into regulatory text to determine when State-required benefits require defrayal, with proposed effectiveness beginning in PY 2027 (soliciting comment on PY 2028).

rubrics_metrics.name: State defrayal responsibility when benefit is not EHB
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State-required benefit does not satisfy the proposed standard at §155.170(a)(1), the State would be required to defray the costs of that benefit by making payments to individual enrollees or to the QHP issuer on behalf of enrollees in accordance with paragraph (b) of §155.170.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QHP issuers would be required to update plan filings beginning in PY 2027 to reflect that the benefit is no longer covered as an EHB and should not be included in the percentage of premium attributable to EHB for calculating APTC; States could avoid defrayal by repealing or limiting market applicability of the State requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of benefits classified as in addition to EHB
rubrics_metrics.description: State-required benefits that are in addition to EHB would not be subject to the rules applicable to EHB, including the prohibition on discrimination (§156.125), the annual limitation on cost sharing (§156.130), and restrictions on annual or lifetime dollar limits (§147.126).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change affects consumer protections associated with EHB status and could also affect self-insured group plans, large-group fully insured plans, BHPs, and Medicaid ABPs that reference a State's EHB-benchmark plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy rationale for reverting to pre-2025 defrayal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS proposes reverting to the standard prior to the 2025 Payment Notice because treating benefits in an EHB-benchmark plan as EHB increases premiums and Federal APTC costs and disproportionately harms unsubsidized enrollees, incentivizing States to enact mandates and select EHB-benchmark plans that shift costs to the Federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed reversion seeks to preserve affordability for unsubsidized enrollees and prevent accumulation of State-required benefits being treated as EHB without State defrayal.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE standards of conduct for agents, brokers, and web-brokers (§155.220(j)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers assisting with or facilitating enrollment in a manner that constitutes enrollment through an FFE or SBE-FP must provide consumers with correct information and refrain from misleading marketing (§155.220(j)(2)(i)); document that the consumer (or their authorized representative) has reviewed and confirmed eligibility application information is accurate (§155.220(j)(2)(ii)); and document the consumer's consent prior to facilitating enrollments (§155.220(j)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards are intended to protect consumers and ensure proper administration of Exchanges; HHS has observed abusive practices (false attestations, manipulated income, wrong addresses, enrolling deceased consumers) and documentation failures (missing agent name, date, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of HHS-approved consumer consent and application review forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to require agents, brokers, and web-brokers to use the HHS-approved and -created consumer consent form to meet eligibility application review and consent documentation requirements, eliminating broad allowances on format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation would clarify what types of actions constitute a consumer 'taking an action' to execute the form; this aims to reduce documentation lacking required information and to standardize consumer-facing language/format that can otherwise be confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documentation content for consent and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation showing consumer review and confirmed accuracy and consent must include required elements such as explanation of attestations; required dates; name of assisting agent/broker/web-broker or agency; an affirmative response from the consumer; review of all application information; name of the consumer or authorized representative; and scope, duration, and purpose of consent including rescission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing or incorrect documentation can harm consumers (incorrect eligibility determinations, tax liabilities, lack of plan correspondence) and hinder Exchange operations; HHS has found frequent noncompliance in various documentation formats (paper/audio).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable and unacceptable consumer actions to establish review/consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal would amend §155.220(j)(2)(ii)(A) to describe acceptable and unacceptable actions that a consumer (or authorized representative) can take to allow the agent, broker, or web-broker to demonstrate confirmation of review of eligibility application information, and redesignate related subparagraphs accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification is intended to reduce variable interpretations and ensure the consumer 'takes an action' that creates a record meeting regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement mechanisms for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS may suspend or terminate an agent's, broker's, or web-broker's Exchange agreement(s) in circumstances involving fraud or abusive conduct or sufficiently severe noncompliance under §155.220(g) and (h); HHS conducts documentation reviews and may provide Technical Assistance (TA) or pursue enforcement actions based on findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation review findings (e.g., missing required elements) drive next steps, including TA or enforcement; failure to provide compliant documentation may result in formal corrective actions from HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of enrollment conduct from marketing and new marketing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to separate conduct related to consumer enrollment from conduct related to consumer marketing at §155.220(j)(2)(i) and to introduce new marketing requirements in redesignated §155.220(j)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aims to address observed abusive, misleading, and coercive marketing practices and to more clearly regulate marketing activities distinct from enrollment assistance.
